```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

**teal_neue** (R package `teal.neue`) brings the exploratory, safety and
efficacy analyses of a clinical trial together in a single
[teal](https://insightsengineering.github.io/teal/) app. It combines the three
*teal.gallery* templates (kept for reference in `inst/templates/`) on top of a
cached data pipeline, with a modernised but still recognisably teal look.

## Run the app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(teal.neue)
run_app()
```

From the project folder you can also open `app.R` in RStudio and press
**Run App** (it loads the package with `pkgload` and calls `run_app()`).

The first launch builds the data (a few seconds); later launches in the same
R session are served from memory, and new sessions from the disk cache.

## A tour of the app

| Tab | What it shows | Starting population |
|---|---|---|
| App Info | Sections, data source, packages | - |
| Data Table, Variable Browser | All datasets | All subjects |
| TLG Catalog | Every table, listing and graph of the TLG Catalog, one page per topic | As in the catalog (per output) |
| Exploratory Analysis | Distributions, outliers, associations, regression, PCA, ... | All subjects |
| Safety Analysis | Demographics, adverse events, labs, exposure, vitals, ECG, concomitant medication | Safety population (`SAFFL == "Y"`) |
| Efficacy Analysis | Forest plots, Kaplan-Meier, response, time-to-event, Cox, logistic, MMRM, ANCOVA | Intent-to-treat (`ITTFL == "Y"`) |

* **Filters are module-specific.** Sex and age filters apply everywhere;
  each safety module also starts on the safety population and each efficacy
  module on the intent-to-treat population, exactly as in the source
  templates. Changing a shared filter updates every module that uses it.
* **Show R code** in any module gives runnable code: it starts with
  `teal.neue::load_teal_neue_data()` with the data-source settings written out, so it
  reproduces the same data in a fresh R session.
* **Dark mode**: the sun/moon button in the header switches the whole app
  between light and dark colours. The app starts in light mode, and the
  browser remembers your choice.
* **Header badge**: shows the data source and the number of subjects.

## The TLG Catalog

The **TLG Catalog** tab reproduces the outputs of the
[TLG Catalog](https://insightsengineering.github.io/tlg-catalog/stable/tlg-index.html)
on the app's data: one page per topic (Adverse Events, Concomitant
Medications, Lab Results, Efficacy, Pharmacokinetics, ...), with the tables,
listings and graphs of that topic in a searchable list on the left. Select an
output (click, or use the arrow keys) to compute it on the filtered data.

* **Show R code** gives the complete code: the data loading, the filters and
  the output's code, written in the catalog's style (tern, rtables, rlistings).
* **Catalog page** opens the output's page in the TLG Catalog.
* A few outputs need datasets the app does not load (ADPC, ADPP, ADAB, ADMH,
  ADHY); they use the *random.cdisc.data* examples for the same patients, as
  noted on their page.

## The data in the console

`run_app()` copies every analysis dataset into the Global Environment, so after
closing the app you can explore them directly:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
head(ADSL)
table(ADAE$AEDECOD)
```

Without the app:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
neue <- load_teal_neue_data(cache_global = TRUE)
names(neue$datasets)
```

Turn the copy off with `options(teal_neue.cache_global = FALSE)` or
`run_app(cache_global = FALSE)`.

## Settings

Everything is configured with R options (see `?teal_neue_options`) or the
equivalent arguments of `run_app()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# freshly generated synthetic data: 200 subjects, seed 7
run_app(source = "synthetic", synthetic = list(N = 200, seed = 7))

# your own ADaM data as parquet files
run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "path/to/adam")

# force a rebuild of the cached data
options(teal_neue.refresh_cache = TRUE)
```

See `vignette("data-sources", package = "teal.neue")` for the data sources, the
data contract and the cache.

## Look and feel

The app keeps teal's structure and its standard Bootstrap 5 theme. A
stylesheet and one script on top of it add:

* **A home page**: click the logo (or press `H`). *Study at a glance*
  summarises the study by arm: key figures, demographics (age, sex, race),
  safety (subjects with any, serious or severe adverse events, deaths, the
  most frequent events) and efficacy (overall survival curves, response
  rates). Point at an arm to highlight it in every widget, hover the
  survival curves to read them at any time, and follow a widget's link to
  the module that goes into detail. These figures describe the whole study,
  before any filter; the modules are where filtered, reproducible analyses
  happen.
* **A command bar**: press `Ctrl+K` (`Cmd+K` on a Mac), `/`, or click the
  search field in the header. Before you type, *Where to?* shows every
  module in its category, nested as in the menus. Type a few letters of a module
  (`km`, `ae grade`), a TLG output ID (`aet02`) or an action (`>dark`).
  `Enter` opens it; `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` opens it in a new browser tab.
* **Where am I**: the header shows the path of the current module (for
  example *Safety Analysis / Adverse Events / AE Summary*); click a part of it
  to see the other modules of that group.
* **Links to every view**: the address bar follows the app
  (`.../#/efficacy-analysis/kaplan-meier-plot`), so views can be bookmarked
  and shared, and the browser's back button goes to the previous view.
* **Output tools**: hover a plot to expand it (zoom with the wheel, drag to
  pan), pin it, compare it, copy it or download it; hover a table to copy it
  for Excel or download it as CSV.
* **Comparison**: pin a plot, change a filter, then choose *Compare*: swipe
  a divider between the two versions, put them side by side, or show their
  difference (what changed keeps its colour, the rest turns white). Pins stay
  in a tray (`P`) for the session.
* **Keyboard shortcuts** for everything; press `?` to see them.
* **A calm, precise look** ("Instrument"): ruled white panels on a dot-grid
  canvas, one teal accent, the system font (Inter elsewhere) for text and
  JetBrains Mono for dataset names, IDs and numbers; a quiet tint per
  category (blue for Exploratory, terracotta for Safety, green for Efficacy,
  violet for the TLG Catalog); a dark mode that works.
* **Appearance** (the sliders button, or `A`): text size, spacing, accent,
  corners, contrast, canvas and motion, remembered by the browser.
* **Plots**: an editorial look for every ggplot2 module (large titles, facet
  labels as headings, a graded ink scale, no tick marks) and
  `theme_minimal()` as the default theme of the exploratory plots. Both are
  applied through teal's own settings, so "Show R code" reproduces the plots
  exactly. In dark mode, plots stay white paper.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(teal_neue.color_mode = "dark")  # default mode for first-time visitors ("light")
options(teal_neue.motion = FALSE)       # no animations
options(teal_neue.ggtheme = "bw")       # another default plot theme (NULL: module defaults)
options(teal_neue.style = FALSE)        # the plain teal look of the source templates
```

To change the plot typography, set teal's own option, which teal_neue then
leaves alone:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(teal.ggplot2_args = teal.widgets::ggplot2_args(
  labs = list(caption = "MY STUDY"),
  theme = teal_neue_plot_theme_args()
))
```
